title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will … Monks, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will.”

title: “Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks,…
content: “Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks, is just the five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome is just the five hindrances. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome, monks, is just the four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world; dwells contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome is just the four foundations of mindfulness.”

title: Elder Rājadatta: A monk came to a charnel ground, Saw a woman’s body Abandoned there, Discarded in the cemetery, Food for worms. Some become disenchanted…
content:
Elder Rājadatta:

A monk came to a charnel ground,
Saw a woman’s body
Abandoned there,
Discarded in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

Some become disenchanted
Seeing such a miserable corpse.
In me, sensual desire arose —
Blind, I was bound.

Faster than boiling rice,
I left that place.
Mindful, clearly comprehending,
I came, sat to one side.

Then I attended to it,
Reflecting wisely —
The danger became clear,
I dwelt in disenchantment.

And my mind was liberated.
Seeing the Dhamma as it is,
I attained the three true knowledges,
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

title: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out…
content: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out any of its limbs or its neck, I will seize it right there, break it, and eat it.’ But, monks, because the tortoise did not stretch out any limb or its neck, the jackal became disenchanted with the tortoise and left, not having gained an opportunity. So too, monks, Māra constantly and relentlessly stands in ambush for you, thinking: ‘Perhaps I can gain an opportunity through the eye … through the tongue … through the mind.’ Therefore, monks, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the eye, practice restraint of the eye. When you hear a sound … smell an odor … taste a flavor … feel a touch … cognize a phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the mind, practice restraint of the mind. Monks, when you live guarding the sense faculties, Māra will become disenchanted with you and leave, not gaining an opportunity, just like the jackal with the tortoise.”

title: Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña: I am exceedingly joyful, Having heard the supreme Dhamma, The Dhamma taught for dispassion, Completely without clinging. In this world of a round…
content:
Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña:

I am exceedingly joyful,
Having heard the supreme Dhamma,
The Dhamma taught for dispassion,
Completely without clinging.

In this world of a round earth,
With many colors and forms,
Bewildering the mind —
Thus I thought:
The sign of beauty is very enticing,
Connected with lust.

As wind blows away dust,
As rain settles it down,
Thoughts become stilled
When seen with wisdom.

All conditioned things are impermanent —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All conditioned things are suffering —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All phenomena are not-self —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

title: Elder Nun Selā: You will not escape, You will not escape this world. What use is this practice of seclusion to you? Enjoy sensual pleasures…
content:
Elder Nun Selā:

You will not escape,
You will not escape this world.
What use is this practice of seclusion to you?
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
Do not have regrets later.

Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears —
They cut the aggregates to pieces.
What you call the pleasure of life —
For me, that sensual pleasure
Is no longer enticing.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed.
The mass of darkness,
The blinding darkness, has been shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are Māra,
You are defeated.

title: “Good is restraint over the eye, Good is restraint over the ear, Good is restraint over the nose, Good is restraint over the tongue.” “Good…
content:
“Good is restraint over the eye,
Good is restraint over the ear,
Good is restraint over the nose,
Good is restraint over the tongue.”

“Good is restraint over the body,
Good is restraint over speech,
Good is restraint over the mind,
Good is restraint everywhere.
A monk restrained everywhere
Is freed from all suffering.”

“One who controls his hands and feet,
Controls his speech and his head,
Delights in inner seclusion,
Is content, lives alone —
Him they call a monk.”

title: “And what, Ānanda, is the perception of peril? Here, Ānanda, a monk, going to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an…
content: “And what, Ānanda, is the perception of peril? Here, Ānanda, a monk, going to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, reflects: ‘This body is of much suffering, of much peril. Various diseases arise in this body, such as: eye disease, ear disease, nose disease, tongue disease, body disease, head disease, ear-edge disease, mouth disease, tooth disease, cough, asthma, catarrh, fever, aging, abdominal pain, fainting, dysentery, colic, cholera, leprosy, boils, eczema, tuberculosis, epilepsy, skin disease, itch, scab, ringworm, scabies, blood-bile disorder, diabetes, hemorrhoids, cancer, sores, ulcerations; diseases born of bile, born of phlegm, born of wind, born of the combination of humors; diseases born of change of season, born of improper behavior, born of sudden assault, born of the result of kamma; cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, urination.’ Thus he dwells contemplating peril in this body.”

title: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But,…
content: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the defilement of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively suffering, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings would not become lustful for form. But because form is happiness, Mahāli, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings become lustful for form. Through lust, they are bound; through being bound, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are defiled.”

title: - “Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the reason why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth,…
content: - “Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the reason why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, do not indulge in sensual pleasures and live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully?” - “Great king, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has said: ‘Come, monks, regarding those who are like mothers, establish a mother’s mind. Regarding those who are like sisters, establish a sister’s mind. Regarding those who are like daughters, establish a daughter’s mind.’ This, great king, is the cause, this is the reason why these young monks … live the holy life completely.”
